Figure.alt: þÿAt the bottom of a canyon, a caster stands in a circular sigil around an enormous red crystal swirling with power We look down from the edge of the steep, grey canyon. At the bottom are twelve enormous square, broken stone obelisks engraved with runes, forming a circle. Between them is a ringed circular desigm,. In the upper right, a red-robed caster stands, a quarter the height of the smallest obelisk. They face an enormous red crystalline structure, taller than all of the obelisks, which glows yellow and swirls with red power.

Story.Body: A terrain object is an element placed in an encounter that alters tactics on the battlefield, allowing the Director to better theme an encounter. Terrain objects range from hazards that provide tempting targets for forced movement, to fieldworks and siege engines that provide a locational advantage, to supernatural objects that an entire encounter can be built around.
Each terrain object is set up in a stat block, but this stat block format is different than for monsters. The following sections explain what you’ll find in a terrain object stat block.

Each dynamic terrain object has an encounter value cost, just like monsters in an encounter. Some objects, particularly environmental hazards, have a cost representing an area, such as a 10 × 10-square section of terrain. A hazard can always be smaller than that indicated size.

Terrain objects have either a fixed amount of Stamina or an amount of Stamina per square, depending on their nature and size. If an object has an amount of Stamina per square, it can be partially destroyed square by square.

Terrain objects either have a standard size (for example, 1M) or a size noted as squares of terrain or material. If a terrain object’s size is noted as squares, a creature can move through that terrain object but might trigger the object’s effects. Many terrain objects sized in squares are difficult terrain, as noted in the object’s size entry.
Some terrain objects have a defined direction indicating how they are placed, such as archer’s stakes having a front side.

Most terrain objects can be deactivated under certain circumstances. The Sabotage skill is generally applicable for tests made to deactivate mechanisms and siege engines, while traps might allow different skills to be used depending on their setup—Alchemy to deactivate a pool of flammable oil, Nature to deactivate a spiked pit trap in a forest, Magic or Psionics to deactivate a supernatural object, and so forth. Disabling a supernatural object requires a more intricate process detailed in each object’s stat block.
Once a terrain object is deactivated, the Director determines what must be done to reset it and how long it takes to do so.

Terrain objects typically activate when a creature enters their space or when the object is interacted with in a specific way. Unless otherwise noted, there is no limit to how often a terrain object can activate.

Some terrain objects, particularly traps and other objects that are set up by creatures, are set to activate only in response to creatures or objects of a particular size. For example, smaller creatures such as goblins and kobolds typically calibrate their traps for size 1M and larger creatures, making those traps safe for smaller creatures to pass through.

Many area terrain objects activate when a creature enters their area without shifting. If such a terrain object is difficult terrain, remember that creatures can’t usually shift through difficult terrain without having a trait or feature that allows them to do so.
Each terrain object’s effect entry defines what happens when the object is triggered.
Some terrain objects can be upgraded to create additional effects. If a terrain object has a size in squares, the upgrade cost is paid on a square-by-square basis unless otherwise noted.
Story.Body_Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 You find all hidden terrain objects adjacent to you.
2 You find all hidden terrain objects within 5 squares of you.
3 You find all hidden terrain objects within 10 squares of you.
Story.Body: Some terrain objects have an Allied Awareness trait noting benefits and options available to creatures who have familiarity and training with the object. If a creature is aware of a terrain object and has sufficient time to study it, they gain the object’s Allied Awareness benefits at the Director’s determination.
Environmental hazards represent natural elements that creatures (typically creatures defending a location) have channeled, cultivated, or otherwise placed to give them an edge in an encounter.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This thicket features close-growing vines tipped with sharp thorns.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 3 per square Size: One or more squares of difficult terrain
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Each square of brambles must be individually destroyed.
A creature enters a square of brambles without shifting.
Story.Ability_Data_Space:
Effect: A creature takes 1 damage per square of brambles they
enter.

Poisonous Thorns (+1 EV) The brambles are poisonous. Any crea - ture who takes damage from brambles is also bleeding
(save ends).

Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
This beehive is full of angry bees who swarm and attack with
little provocation.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The beehive can’t be deactivated. If it takes damage or is destroyed, the hive unleashes a swarm of bees.
A creature enters the hive’s space or an adjacent space without shifting.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The hive is removed from the encounter map and a swarm of bees is placed in one square of the space of the triggering crea - ture. Any creature who starts their turn in the swarm’s space takes 3 poison damage. At the start of each round, the swarm moves 1 square and its size increases by 1 square (to 2 squares by 2 squares, 3 squares by 3 squares, and so forth), preferring squares in a crea - ture’s space. After 3 rounds, the swarm dissipates.

Concealed Hive (+1 EV) The hive is hidden until the swarm is
unleashed.
Story.Ability_Body: Killer Bees (+2 EV) The bees are a particularly aggressive and dangerous species. The hive triggers even if a creature shifts into or while adjacent to it, and the swarm deals 1d6 + 3 poison damage.

Figure.alt: þÿA tangle of green, red-thorned vines More than a dozen thick, rope-like, kelly green vines covered in long, thin, rose-like, blood-red thorns stretch out in all directions, mostly away from us, from the lower right to the upper left. Some vines are closer to us, some are further away. Some are higher up, others, lower down, are faded, almost as if through mist. They meet just above the middle of the page to twist together in a tangled knot before continuing off in other directions.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A shallow, frozen patch of water features ice thick enough that it won’t break, but its surface is slick and treacherous to navigate.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 3 per square Size: One or more squares of difficult terrain
Immunity: 5 to all damage except fire damage
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Destroying a square of the frozen pond turns the square into shallow icy water.
A creature or object enters a square of the frozen pond without shifting.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Slippery Surface ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object enters a square of the frozen pond without shifting.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 Push 1 in the direction the target was moving

2 Push 2 in the direction the target was moving; a
<1] slowed (save ends)
3 Push 3 in the direction the target was moving; a<2] prone and can’t stand (save ends)
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The triggering creature’s movement ends, then they are force moved. If the target triggered this ability by being force moved, this ability gains an edge and any remaining forced move - ment distance is added to the ability’s forced movement. The ability’s forced movement doesn’t trigger the ability again.

Thin Ice (+1 EV) The ice covering the pond is thin and the water is deeper. Whenever a creature or object enters or falls prone in a square of the frozen pond, that square is destroyed and replaced with icy water. The Icy Water ability replaces Slippery Surface.

Any creature who starts their turn in the icy water takes 1 cold damage. If the water is deep enough, a creature can swim beneath the surface of the frozen pond, but takes this cold damage while doing so.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A creature or object enters or falls prone in a square of the frozen pond.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The triggering creature’s movement ends, then they are force moved if applicable.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This shallow pool bubbles with acid or some other corrosive liquid.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 12 per square Size: One or more squares of difficult terrain
Immunity: 20 to all damage except cold or fire damage
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The pool must be completely destroyed.
A creature or object enters the corrosive pool or starts their turn there. The liquid in the pool is also highly volatile (see Explosive Reaction below).
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: A creature or object takes 3 acid damage if they start their turn in the pool, and takes 3 acid damage for each square of the pool they enter.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e 3 burst x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: The pool takes fire damage.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 3 fire damage; m<1] the target is burning (save ends)
2 6 fire damage; m<2] the target is burning (save ends)
3 9 fire damage; m<3] the target is burning (save ends)
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The liquid in the pool is consumed. This ability has a dou - ble edge against any target in the pool. A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round. Any target with acid weakness takes extra damage from this ability and while burning as if the fire damage were acid damage.
Story.Ability_Body: Allies who have weapons are equipped with torches. Any ally can use a maneuver to throw a torch up to 5 squares and deal 1 fire damage to the pool, triggering Explosive Reaction.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
When this patch of sand is stepped on, it is revealed to be a
slurry saturated by water—and ready to draw creatures down
to their doom.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: — Size: One or more squares
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature or object enters the quicksand or starts their turn there.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Grasping Depths ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object enters the quicksand or starts their turn there.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This ability takes a bane if a triggering creature shifted into the quicksand. A character who starts their turn restrained this way is suffocating.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The quicksand is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A patch of blisteringly hot molten rock wells up from the ground, threatening anyone who gets close to it.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 12 per square Size: One or more squares of difficult terrain
Immunity: 20 to all damage except cold damage
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Each square of lava must be individually destroyed.
A creature or object enters the lava or starts their turn there, or starts their turn adjacent to the lava.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Liquid Hot Magma ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Melee 1 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object enters the lava or starts their turn there, or starts their turn adjacent to the lava.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 5 fire damage; m<1] the target is burning (save ends)
2 9 fire damage; m<2] the target is burning (save ends)
3 12 fire damage; m<3] the target is burning (save ends)
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: If the target is adjacent to lava but not in it, this ability takes a bane. A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round.
Magma Flow (+4 EV) The lava is flowing! At the start of each round, add one square of lava adjacent to an existing square of lava.

Story.Body: Fieldworks represent temporary military fortifications meant to give defenders an edge in an encounter.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: Colorful mushrooms or lovely flowering plants release a cloud of spores or pollen when disturbed, causing creatures to fall into a magical slumber.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 3 per square Size: One or more squares
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Each square of plants must be individually destroyed.
A creature starts their turn in the area of the toxic plants, or enters a square of toxic plants without shifting.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Sleep Spores ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Magic, Melee, Strike Free triggered action
e Melee 0 x The triggering creature
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A creature starts their turn in the area of the toxic plants, or enters a square of toxic plants without shifting.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: While dazed this way, a target who starts their turn in the area of the toxic plants falls prone and can’t stand.
Poisonous Spores (+2 EV) Any creature dazed by this hazard takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of their turns.

Carnivorous Plants (+2 EV) The plants are carnivorous and attempt to slowly digest any creature who falls among them. Any creature who starts their turn prone in the area takes 4 acid
damage.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A series of sharp stakes have been placed point-out to protect defenders against charges and other direct attacks.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 3 per square Size: One or more squares of difficult terrain
Direction: One side of the stakes is defined as the front.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Each square of stakes must be individually destroyed.
A creature enters an area of stakes from the front.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The triggering creature takes 2 damage per square of stakes they enter. If they are force moved into an area of stakes, they take an additional 3 damage.
Poison (+2 EV) The tips of the stakes have poison applied to them. Any creature who takes damage from the stakes also takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of their turns (save ends).

Sticky (+3 EV) A sticky slime or webbing has been applied to the stakes and the ground between them. Any creature who enters an area of stakes triggers the Sticky Stakes ability in addition to suffering the stakes’ other effects.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Melee, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object enters an area of sticky stakes.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Allies of this object ignore the difficult terrain created by the stakes, take no damage from moving through the stakes unless they are force moved, and have cover while in an area of archer’s stakes.

Figure.alt: þÿA collection of red-spined, green fruit, one of which has cracked open to release a yellow gas.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A set of spring-loaded steel jaws stands ready to snap shut when stepped on.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a bear trap can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the trap and is affected as if in its space.
2 The trap is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The trap is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The bear trap is calibrated to be triggered by creatures or objects of a particular size or larger. The trap triggers when a creature or object of the appropriate size enters its space.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: A triggering creature or object ends their movement and is targeted by the Bear Trap ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Melee, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object of the appropriate size enters the trap’s space.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The target shifts 1 square away from the trap.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The bear trap must be manually reset.
Chain (+1 EV) The bear trap is attached to the ground by a steel chain. A target who would be made slowed by the trap is restrained instead.
Story.Ability_Body: The bear trap is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A patch of flammable oil or pitch on the ground is ready to be ignited.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: — Size: One or more squares
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a patch of flammable oil can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature ignites the oil and is affected as if in its area.
2 The oil temporarily ignites before safely burning out, and the creature takes 3 fire damage and is burning (save ends).
3 The oil is rendered safe and can’t be ignited.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature or object in a square of oil takes fire damage, or a creature or object enters a square of burning oil or starts their turn there.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The triggering creature or object takes 3 fire damage and is burning (save ends). A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round.
Concealed Oil (+1 EV) The oil is hidden until it ignites.
Story.Ability_Body: Allies who have weapons are equipped with torches. Any ally can use a maneuver to throw a torch up to 5 squares and ignite the flammable oil.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A reinforced metal shield embedded in the ground acts as cover for the creature controlling it.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a pavise shield controlled by another creature can make a Might test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature controlling the shield retains control of it and can make an opportunity attack against the creature making the test.
2 The creature controlling the shield retains control of it.
3 The creature making the test grabs the shield and takes control of it.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: While a creature has the pavise shield grabbed, they have cover and take half damage from abilities whose line of effect extends through the shield. The pavise shield takes the other half of the damage.
Movement: While a creature has a pavise shield grabbed, their speed is halved and they move the shield like a grabbed creature.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A cavity in a floor, wall, or ceiling might hold hidden threats.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: — Size: One or more squares
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a hidey-hole can make a Might test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll:
2 The hidey-hole collapses but the creature is slowed
(save ends).

3 The hidey-hole collapses and can no longer be used until
repaired.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature starts the encounter in the hidey-hole or ends their turn there.
Story.Ability_Data_Space:
Effect: The triggering creature can attempt to hide as a free
triggered action.

Network (+1 EV per hidey-hole) The hidey-hole is connected to a tunnel network. A creature familiar with the network can move from one hidey-hole to any space adjacent to a connected hid - ey-hole if they have movement available equal to the straight-line distance to that space. A creature unfamiliar with the network can use a maneuver to make a hard Intuition test to discover a connected hidey-hole.

Figure.alt: þÿAn adventurer climbs down a wooden ladder into a cellar, while a lantern-bearing person at the top waves to them The older, balding, ligjht-medium skinned human at the top of the ladder wears a beige shirt and a tan apron.. They smile and raise their arm in a wave, illuminated by the lantern in their other hand. A light-skinned, red-haired adventurer in a stained white-and-blue-striped doublet, brown pants, and boots, weating a shortsword at their belt, climbs down the wooden ladder, their back to us, toward a cellar full of wooden barrels and crates.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A rope snare is set to grab a target, leaving them hanging up - side down.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a snare trap can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the trap and is affected as if in its space.
2 The trap is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The trap is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The snare trap is calibrated to be triggered by creatures or objects of a particular size or larger. The trap triggers when a creature or object of the appropriate size enters its space.
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Effect: A triggering creature or object ends their movement and is targeted by the Snare ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Melee, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A creature or object of the appropriate size enters the trap’s space.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The target shifts 1 square away from the snare.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: A creature restrained this way is vertical pulled 2 squares and suspended in the air by the snare line. On a successful save, the snare is cut or breaks and the creature falls to the ground. The snare must be manually reset.

Net Trap (+1 EV) The snare becomes a net that can wrap up mul - tiple targets. The net has 3 Stamina and fills an area of 3 squares by 3 squares. The Snare ability loses its existing keywords, gains the Area keyword, and targets each creature or object in the area. The trap can be triggered by a target moving through one specific square, or by requiring multiple squares to be moved through. Any creature who makes their save to end the restrained effect ends that effect for all targets, who all fall to the ground.
Story.Ability_Body: The snare trap is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A pit dug into the ground is filled with spikes, and camouflaged to avoid detection.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 6 Size: One or more squares
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a spike trap can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the trap and is affected as if in its area.
2 The trap is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The trap is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: The spike trap is calibrated to be triggered by creatures or objects of a particular size or larger. The trap triggers when a creature or object of the appropriate size enters its area.
Effect: The Spike Trap ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Melee 0 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A creature or object of the appropriate size enters the trap’s area.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 3 damage; the target shifts 1 square away from the trap
2 4 damage; the target falls into the pit; a<0] prone
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The target ends their movement when they enter the trap’s area. The pit is typically 2 squares deep. The trap must be manually reset.
Story.Ability_Body: The spike trap is hidden until triggered or detected.

Figure.alt: þÿA club-wielding troll is pinned to a rocky dungeon wall by a claw-lined net The green-grey skinned, tusked troll has a tuft of hair but their head is tilted back and illuminated by flames from a fallen wall sconce's torch in the lower corner in such a way that the color is impossible to decipher. They wear a loincloth and chestplate made of green and brown, steel-lined shields. They are pinned flat against the t cavern wall, almost seeming to be part of it. Their left arm is up and bent, their right, outstretched, holding a club with spikes made of broken sword blades. They are pinned to the wall by a square net with green edges woven with teeth which gauge into both the wall and their flesh.

Story.Body: Mechanisms represent any number of intricate devices that can complicate a battle. Unlike more straightforward traps, a mechanism is often linked to another triggering mechanism that activates it.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A concealed dart thrower hurls missiles at short range.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Direction The dart trap fires in a fixed direction.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a dart trap can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the trap and is targeted by it.
2 The trap is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The trap is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Ability_Body: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Dart ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Ranged, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Ranged 5 x One creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Poison Darts (+2 EV) The darts are tipped with poison. Any crea - ture who takes damage from a dart also takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of their turns (save ends).

Large Darts (+1 EV) Larger, heavier darts impart kinetic force to the trap’s attack. A target of the Dart ability is pushed 1 square on a tier 1 outcome, 2 squares on a tier 2 outcome, or 3 squares on a tier 3 outcome.

Gatling Darts (+4 EV) The dart trap is equipped with multiple bar - rels to launch darts at a high rate of fire. The Dart ability loses the Ranged and Strike and takes the Area keyword, its area becomes a 5 × 1 line within 1, and it deals an extra 1d6 damage.
Story.Ability_Body: The dart trap is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Monster_Role: Column of Blades Level 3 Fortification Defender
Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
A spinning wooden column is affixed with sharp blades to
slash the unwary.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The column of blades must be completely destroyed.
A creature or object moves adjacent to the column of blades.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Spinning Blades ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Melee, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Melee 1 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A creature or object moves within distance of the column.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Stone Column (+1 EV) The column is made of stone and has 8 Stamina.
Metal Column (+1 EV) The column is made of metal and has 11 Stamina.
Concealed (+1 EV) The blades are concealed inside the column, which remains motionless until triggered.
Spiked Flails (+4 EV) Instead of blades, the column is affixed with heavy spiked balls attached by long chains. The Whirling Flails ability replaces Spinning Blades.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Melee, Strike, Weapon Free triggered action
e Melee 2 x The triggering creature or object
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A creature or object moves within distance of the column.
Allies who shift don’t trigger the column. A creature observing an ally shift this way can make an Intuition test to shift in imitation of their movements.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the column and the column’s ability gains an edge.
3 The creature doesn’t trigger the column.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This stone pillar can be toppled onto unsuspecting foes with the right amount of damage or a well-engineered trigger mechanism.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 6 Size: One square that can’t be moved through
Direction: The pillar topples in a preset direction.
Story.Ability_Body: The pillar’s linked trigger must be deactivated.
The pillar is destroyed, or a pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Toppling Pillar ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e 4 × 1 line within 1 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: The pillar is destroyed, or a pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The area is difficult terrain.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Metal Pillar (+1 EV) The pillar is made of metal, has 9 Stamina, and deals 1d6 extra damage.

Multiple Pillars (+3 EV per additional pillar) Multiple pillars can be used to represent a larger toppling object such as a wall. If triggered by destruction, all individual pillars need to be destroyed before the object falls.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A portcullis is hidden in the ceiling of a passage or choke point, waiting to drop when activated.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 9 per square Size: The area of the corridor to be blocked
Typical Space: 2 × 1-square area, up to a 4 × 2-square area
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a portcullis can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the portcullis and is affected as if in its area.
2 The portcullis is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The portcullis is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Ability_Body: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Heavy Gate ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Special x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Body:
Trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is
activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Special: The area of this ability is the area directly beneath the portcullis when it falls.

Effect: The portcullis blocks movement from one side of it to the other. A target slid by the portcullis ends up on one side of it or the other (choose randomly). The portcullis must be manually reset.
Story.Ability_Body: The portcullis is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This mechanism acts as a trigger for another linked mechanism, and is skillfully hidden from view in the floor.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Typical Space: One square, up to a 4 × 4-square area
Story.Body: Link: A pressure plate is linked to another mechanism that it activates when triggered.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a pressure plate can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the pressure plate.
2 The pressure plate is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The pressure plate is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The pressure plate is calibrated to be triggered by creatures or objects of a particular size. The pressure plate triggers when a creature or object of the appropriate size enters its area.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The linked mechanism is activated. A pressure plate auto - matically resets and can be triggered repeatedly.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: Tripwire (−1 EV) The pressure plate is a tripwire, which can trigger once and must be manually reset. A concealed tripwire can be discovered with an easy Intuition test.
The pressure plate is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A counterweighted pulley system can be used to quickly ascend to the top of a wall, scaffold, tower, or other structure.
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a pulley can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 2 The pulley is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The pulley is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Ability_Body: A creature adjacent to the pulley uses a maneuver to release the pulley.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The triggering creature is lifted to the top of the structure the pulley is attached to. The pulley must be manually reset.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature adjacent to the pulley can climb its ropes with an easy Agility test to ascend to the top of the structure it’s attached to.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Looped Chain (+1 EV) Instead of a rope and pulley, the system uses a counterweighted looped chain. A looped chain automati - cally resets and can be triggered repeatedly.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: Set into any surface, this mechanism acts as a trigger for another linked mechanism.
Story.Body: Link: A switch is linked to another mechanism that it activates when triggered.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a switch can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 2 The switch is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The switch is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature adjacent to the switch uses a maneuver to trigger it.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The linked mechanism is activated. A switch automatically resets and can be triggered repeatedly.
Concealed (+1 EV) The switch is hidden.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A heavy wooden ram drops down or swings into the fray, crushing all in its path.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Stamina: 3 per square Size: Any area; the area can’t be moved through
Typical Space: 1 × 3-square area or a 2 × 2-square area
Direction: One side of the ram is defined as the front.
Story.Ability_Body:
As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a ram can make an
Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature triggers the ram and is affected as if in its space.
2 The ram is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The ram is deactivated and doesn’t trigger.
Story.Ability_Body: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Ram ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Special x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Leading_Colon: Trigger: A pressure plate, switch, or other linked trigger is activated.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Special: The area of this ability is the path the ram moves through from its starting position.
Effect: A target slid by the ram ends up on one side of it or the other (choose randomly). The ram must be manually reset.
Stone (+1 EV) The ram is made of stone, has 6 Stamina per square, and deals an extra 1d3 damage.
Metal (+2 EV) The ram is made of metal, has 9 Stamina per square, and deals an extra 1d6 damage.
Repeating (+1 EV) The ram automatically resets at the start of each round.
Rapid Repeating (+3 EV) The ram automatically resets at the start of each turn.
Story.Ability_Body: Multiple Rams (+3 EV per additional ram) Multiple rams can be used to represent a larger mechanism, such as a stack of tumbling logs.
The ram is hidden until triggered or detected.

Story.Body: Power fixtures are especially potent fortifications for solo creatures and smaller strike forces. The more of these terrain objects that occupy the field of battle, the worse things get for the attacking side.

Story.Monster_Role: Tree of Might Level 5 Hazard Hexer
Story.Ability_Body: A gnarled tree has unearthed roots that writhe and curl.
Story.Stat_Block_Data: Immunity: 5 to all damage except corruption or fire damage
Story.Ability_Body: The tree of might must be completely destroyed.

At the start of each round while the tree of might is intact, each enemy touching the ground in the encounter area who has m<0] takes 10 corruption damage, and the tree of might grows a fruit. The potency increases by 1 each subsequent round.

Once per round, any creature adjacent to the tree of might can take a fruit from the tree and eat it (no action required). The creature gains 10 temporary Stamina and has their Might score increased by 1 (to a maximum of 6) until the end of the encounter.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
An empowering monument to a higher power enables
a villain’s machinations.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The holy idol must be completely destroyed.

At the start of each round while the holy idol is intact, the Director gains a d6 that lasts until the end of the round. When a Director-controlled creature deals or takes damage, the Director can roll the d6 to increase the damage the creature deals or reduce the damage the creature takes by an amount equal to the roll (to a minimum of 2 damage). If multiple idols are in play, only one d6 can be applied to a single instance of damage.

Figure.alt: þÿBroken shards of multi-hued crystal orbit a large diamond-shaped chunk of orange-and-blue crystal

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A massive humming crystal makes the air around it feel thick.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The psionic shard must be completely destroyed.
A psionic shard is attuned to one side in an encounter. While a psionic shard is intact, any damage dealt to each ally of the shard in the encounter is halved.
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: The shard is destroyed.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The shard releases a shockwave channeled through each creature affected by Psionic Barrier. Each ally in the encounter is dazed until the end of their next turn.

Story.Body: Siege engines are powerful weapons that require a team of creatures to operate and move. These weapons can scale in size from smaller field artillery to massive mechanisms that can destroy buildings.

Rather than siege engines taking actions on their own, a creature adjacent to the siege engine can use a main action to activate a siege engine ability noted as “Main action (Adjacent creature).” In addition to their primary attack, some siege engines require an adjacent creature main action to reload them once they are used, while others have adjacent creature main actions allowing them to be moved or allowing a creature to improve the engine’s distance and accuracy.
Multiple minions in a squad can activate different aspects of a siege engine using adjacent creature main actions.

Story.Monster_Role: Arrow Launcher Level 2 Siege Engine Artillery
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A small wooden cart uses alchemical rockets to launch up to a hun - dred arrows at a time across a wide area.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an arrow launcher can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Arrow Storm ability.
2 The arrow launcher is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The arrow launcher is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Area, Ranged, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
e 5 cube within 20 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This ability can’t be used again until the arrow launcher is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Body: Effect: The arrow launcher is reloaded, allowing Arrow Storm to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The next use of Arrow Storm gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The arrow launcher and the creature using this action move together up to 3 squares.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Flaming Arrows (+1 EV) Arrow Storm deals fire damage, and can ignite flammable objects in its area.

Screamers (+3 EV) The arrows make a high-pitched screaming noise as they are fired and descend onto their targets. The
Screamers ability replaces Arrow Storm.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Area, Ranged, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
e 5 cube within 20 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This ability can’t be used again until the arrow launcher is reloaded.

Figure.alt: þÿA comet-like projectile sails over a battlefield of infantry squares in front of a city Coming directly at us and taking up nearly half the page from the center-right is a comet-like projectile formed of the orange-edged, glowing blue-purple of agonized souls, whose screaming skull-faces make it appear almost like a crater-filled moon. In the background, at the center-top of the page, is a city of spired buildings forming a rocket-like triangular shape. In front of the city are four rows and several columns, partially obscured by the comet, of infantry squares. Glowing blue-purple soul-projectiles arc towards us, launched from various locations. In the foreground, just aabove the lower-right corner, a projectlle impacts in a huge explosion of blue and purple, surrounded by flaming orange embers and black smoke, The impact throws back soldiers a tenth of its size, easily engulfing a square. In the lower left corner is the smoldering crater of a previous impact, only a few small blue-purple flames and grey-black smoke left behind.

Story.Monster_Role: Boiling Oil Cauldron Level 3 Fortification Defender
Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
A large cauldron of boiling oil stands ready to be poured
onto enemies.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a boiling oil cauldron can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Boiling Oil ability.
2 The boiling oil cauldron is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The boiling oil cauldron is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e 3 cube within 1 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: If the boiling oil is poured down on targets from above, it has high ground and gains an edge on the power roll. A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round. This ability can’t be used again until the boiling oil cauldron is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Body: Effect: The boiling oil cauldron is reloaded, allowing Boiling Oil to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This massive counterweighted engine hurls a heavy projectile for a devastating assault.
Story.Ability_Body: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a catapult can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Arcing Shot ability.
2 The catapult is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The catapult is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Area, Ranged, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
e 3 cube within 20 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: Line of effect for this ability is an arc that can be traced over obstacles between the catapult and the target area. This ability can’t be used again until the catapult is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Body: Effect: The catapult is reloaded, allowing Arcing Shot to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The next use of Arcing Shot gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The catapult and the creature using this action move together up to 2 squares.
Story.Ability_Data_Space:
Air Assault (+2 EV) The side fielding the catapult has trained their forces to safely use the siege engine to launch them across the
battlefield. As an adjacent creature main action, the catapult can be used to vertical push 10 any ally of size 1L or less. If the ally lands in an unoccupied space, they take no damage.

Flammable (+2 EV) Arcing Shot deals fire damage, and the area of that ability is on fire until the end of the encounter. Any creature who enters the area for the first time in a round or starts their turn there takes 2 fire damage.

Story.Monster_Role: Field Ballista Level 2 Siege Engine Artillery
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A massive crossbow fires thick metal bolts with devastating effect.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to a field ballista can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Release Bolt ability.
2 The field ballista is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The field ballista is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Ranged, Strike, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
e Ranged 20 x One creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This ability can’t be used again until the field ballista is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Body: Effect: The field ballista is reloaded, allowing Release Bolt to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The next use of Release Bolt gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The field ballista and the creature using this action move together up to 3 squares.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Penetrating Bolt (+2 EV) The field ballista targets the nearest two additional creatures or objects in a straight line beyond the initial target.

Chain Bolt (+2EV) The field ballista’s bolts are set with heavy chains that wrap around targets. The Chain Bolt ability replaces Release Bolt, and the field ballista gains the Crank the Chain
ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Ranged, Strike, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
e Ranged 20 x One creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This ability can’t be used again until the field ballista is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: Ranged, Strike, Weapon Main action (Adjacent creature)
Story.Ability_Body: Special: The target must be slowed by the field ballista.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: This forced movement triggers opportunity attacks.

Story.Monster_Role: Exploding Mill Wheel Level 3 Siege Engine Artillery
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A massive wooden wheel is loaded with explosives and rolled toward enemy forces or fortifications, ready to explode.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an exploding mill wheel that isn’t rolling can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Roll the Wheel ability.
2 The exploding mill wheel is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The exploding mill wheel is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Once the wheel is rolling, it can’t be deactivated. However, it can be exploded early by destroying it or blocking its movement with a suitably large creature or object.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Special x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: When this ability is used and at the start of every turn thereafter, the exploding mill wheel rolls, moving 2 squares in a straight line. Each creature and object of size 2 or smaller in the area defined by the wheel’s movement is targeted by the follow - ing power roll. A target force moved this way is moved to either side of the wheel, as the Director determines.

If the wheel enters the space of any creature or object of size 3 or larger, or if it is reduced to 0 Stamina, its movement stops and it explodes. Each creature and object in a 5 burst centered on the wheel is targeted by the following power roll.
A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round.

Piloted (+4 EV) The wheel has been fitted with a control mech - anism and a pilot’s seat for a creature of size 1M or smaller. As a move action, the pilot can turn the wheel in any direction while it is moving. As a main action, the pilot can leap out of the pilot’s seat, landing in an adjacent space while the wheel continues moving in a straight line.
Without proper training, determining how to pilot the wheel requires a Reason test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The wheel immediately explodes as if striking a size 3 or larger creature or object.
2 The creature fails to pilot the wheel.
3 The creature can pilot the wheel.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: On a natural 19 or 20, a creature can both pilot the wheel and can disarm its explosives as a maneuver.

Story.Monster_Role: Iron Dragon Level 4 Siege Engine Artillery
Story.Feature_Intro_Text:
A massive metal device uses a bellows system and liquid fuel to
shoot out gouts of flame.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to an iron dragon can make an Agility test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Gout of Flame ability.
2 The iron dragon is deactivated but the creature is slowed (EoT).
3 The iron dragon is deactivated and can’t be used.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e 8 × 2 line within 1 x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 6 damage; a<0] the target is burning (save ends)
2 10 damage; a<1] the target is burning (save ends)
3 13 damage; a<2] the target is burning (save ends)
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: A burning creature takes 1d6 fire damage at the start of each of their turns. A burning object takes 1d6 fire damage at the end of each round. This ability can’t be used again until the iron dragon is reloaded.
Story.Ability_Body: Effect: The iron dragon is reloaded, allowing Gout of Flame to be used again. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The next use of Gout of Flame gains an edge and has a +10 bonus to ranged distance. This action can be used only once per round.
Effect: The iron dragon and the creature using this action move together up to 2 squares

Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A sturdy wooden tower accessed by interior ladders or stairs provides cover and high ground for attackers.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The watchtower must be completely destroyed.
Story.Ability_Body: Creatures who have access to the watchtower’s interior ladders or stairs have high ground and cover against creatures outside the watchtower.
A creature outside and adjacent to the watchtower can gain access to the interior by climbing it as an Agility test or breaking into it with a Might test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 1d6 damage; the creature remains outside the watchtower
2 The creature remains outside the watchtower.
3 The creature gains access to the watchtower.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Ballista Emplacement (+12 EV) The watchtower is equipped with a field ballista that can be used by creatures in the watchtower. The ballista can’t be moved.

Boiling Oil Cauldron (+17 EV) The watchtower is equipped with a boiling oil cauldron that can be used by creatures in the
watchtower.

Spyglass (+2 EV) Any creature in the watchtower can use the spyglass to search for hidden creatures around the tower, gaining an edge on the Intuition test and increasing the distance at which creatures can be spotted to 15 squares.
Stone Tower (+2 EV) The watchtower is reinforced with stone and has 75 Stamina.
Iron Tower (+4 EV) The watchtower is reinforced with stone and iron and has 100 Stamina.

Figure.alt: þÿA green-blue flame glows from the ruins of a watchtower as a ghostly draconian stands guard A crumbling, shattered stone castle stretches out over a mist-shrouded, forested land. Its decimated watchtower is right in front of us. Glowing blue-green flames dance in the ruins, while a draconian, made of the same glowing power, stands atop a crumbling wall, holding a spear and peering outward, continuing their watch.

Story.Body: Infused with magic or psionics, these powerful and esoteric terrain objects can provide a strong environmental threat, or even be the centerpiece of an encounter.

Story.Monster_Role: The Chronal Hypercube Level 3 Relic Controller
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: This unnatural object twists space around it in a reflection of its own unnatural form.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature who has the Psionics skill can deactivate and take control of the chronal hypercube by making a Reason test while within 10 squares of the hypercube.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 2 The creature fails to deactivate the hypercube.
3 The hypercube teleports adjacent to the creature at the start of the next round and becomes an ally to the creature and their allies.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: At the start of each round while the hypercube is present, roll a d10. On a 7 or higher, the hypercube teleports to a square of one ally’s choice within 10 squares and is hidden. While the hypercube is hidden, Psionics is the only skill that can be applied to a test made to find it.
Any ally within 10 squares of the hypercube can teleport when they move. An ally who teleports gains an edge on the next power roll they make.

Story.Sidebar_Body: Supernatural objects are unique in having effects that target or affect enemies and allies. Although supernatural objects don’t (necessarily) have awareness or sapience, their presence in an encounter aligns them clearly with or against the heroes. Unless the Director determines otherwise, the heroes are usually the enemies of a supernatural object.

Story.Monster_Role: The Black Obelisk Level 3 Relic Controller
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: A foreboding obelisk shaped of dark stone harrows the minds and spirits of those around it.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: As a maneuver, a creature adjacent to the black obelisk can make a Reason test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The creature accidentally activates the Your Fears Become Manifest ability, which gains an edge.
2 The creature must make another test to deactivate the obelisk. If they obtain this outcome a second time, they accidentally activate Your Fears Become Manifest.
3 The obelisk is deactivated until the end of the encounter.
Story.Ability_Body: A new round starts.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The Your Fears Become Manifest ability.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Burst 10 x Each enemy in the area
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A new round starts.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The target is pushed 2 squares.

Figure.alt: þÿA complex, glowing object formed of non-Euclidean nesting cubes The Chronal Hypercube is a glowing peach cube radiating iridescent light outward into a darker cube, as dark, blue runed panels stretch yet further outward on rectangular peach prisms, narrower than the cube's sides. The geometry of the cube shifts depending on perspective, with things appearing to shift distance and connections depending on angle and focus.

Story.Monster_Role: The Throne of A’An Level 4 Relic Controller
Story.Feature_Intro_Text: The throne of A’An, sun god of the Antical Protectorate in what is now Vanigar, retains some of her power from the age before she was slain to end the Age of Suns—and plunge the region into eternal winter.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: The throne of A’An can be deactivated only by the current hierophant of A’An (see Sitting on the Throne), who must succeed on a Presence test that takes a bane to do so.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 The hierophant triggers the Nova ability.
2 The hierophant fails to deactivate the throne.
3 The throne is deactivated until the end of the encounter.
Story.Stat_Block_Ability_Header: t Light of the Northern Sun
Story.Stat_Body_Text: In the Age of Suns, there was no darkness and no night. Even among the many suns of that time, the light of A’An was the brightest. The throne of A’An manifests the sun powers of that god, even when no one is seated in it. The following effects always occur within 10 squares of the throne:

LI.LBody: The throne sheds bright light that negates all darkness and con - cealment, and which prevents creatures from being hidden.
Any creature with cold immunity has fire weakness 10.
Any creature who uses an ability that deals cold damage takes 11 fire damage.

Story.Stat_Body_Text: Only a creature attuned to the throne can sit on it. A creature adjacent to the throne can use a main action to attune to it by succeeding on a Presence test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 2 The creature fails to attune to the throne.
3 The creature attunes to the throne and can sit on it.
Story.Stat_Body_Text: A creature seated on the throne becomes the hierophant of A’An and gains the following benefits:

LI.LBody: The hierophant and each of their allies within 10 squares of the throne have fire immunity 10.
The hierophant and each of their allies within 10 squares of the throne can choose to have their abilities deal fire damage instead of their usual damage.
The hierophant has a +5 bonus to stability, and any strike made against them takes a bane unless the attacker is also attuned to the throne.

The hierophant can use the Primordial Flare and
Solar Accretion abilities.

Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e Ranged 20 x One creature or object
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: The target has fire weakness 10 until the start of the hiero - phant’s next turn.
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: A target within distance is made winded or is reduced to 0 Stamina by fire damage.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: If the hierophant is a hero, they gain 3 of their Heroic Resource. If the hierophant is a Director-controlled creature, the Director gains 3 Malice.
Story.Ability_Range__Type__Action_: e 10 burst x Each creature and object in the area
Story.Ability_Body: Trigger: The throne is destroyed or the hierophant obtains a tier 1 outcome on the test to deactivate it.
Story.Ability_Data_Space: Effect: Each target takes 14 fire damage and the Hierophant gains the Incubator of A’An complication (see the sidebar). If there is no hierophant, one creature within 10 squares of the throne chosen by the Director gains this complication.

Story.Sidebar_Body: A shard of the formerly dead sun god A’An incubates within your body, guiding you so that A’An can be restored to her true glory by earning one hundred disciples.

(This complication should be introduced to a campaign only with caution, and with the understanding that all the players are happy to have the party’s agency affected by one of the characters roleplaying a forgotten god.)

Benefit: You have all the abilities of the Sun domain as if you were a conduit of your level. Additionally, you gain fire immunity 5. If you succeed in resurrecting A’An, you will become a saint of A’An.
Drawback: You have cold weakness 5. Whenever you finish a respite and you have not recruited a new disciple of A’An since your last respite, make a Presence test.
Story.Abiilty_Power_Roll: 1 A’An possesses your body until your next respite. You now must roleplay A’An trapped in your form, prioritiz - ing earning new disciples.

Figure.alt: þÿA human knight in gleaming armor and a red cape wields a sword and shield battles attacking warriors The medium-dark-skinned knight has long, dark reddish-brown hair in twists, pulled back. They wear full, gleaming plate armor and a flowing red cape. They lunge forward with a battle cry, their back arm holding a steel buckler, which bashes a light-skinned, brown-bearded enemy with locs, sending them flying backward, and their front arm points a bloodied longsword toward another enemy just to our left, whose fur-trimmed, light-skinned hand peeks into frame. Above the knight's head, the tan castle they defend shatters in a burst of stone. Another knight battles nearby. The ground is strewn with the bare-chested, fur-trimmed corpses of enemies.

Story.Body: A retainer is a type of NPC follower who fights alongside the heroes. Retainer creatures can gain levels just as heroes do, so their battlefield contributions remain relevant as the heroes grow in status and power. A lowly level 1 goblin guide can advance up to level 10 if they adventure with a heroic party for long enough!

The stat blocks in this chapter have the Retainer type next to their level and role. For example, a goblin guide is a level 1 harrier retainer. Some retainers, such as the human warrior or the time raider mind healer, are members of playable ancestries. Others, such as the minotaur gorer, are more monstrous in nature. Additionally, the rules in this chapter allow for the creation of new retainers using nearly any monster as a base creature.

A retainer is a follower of a specific hero. This hero is called the retainer’s mentor, and their player controls that retainer in battle. Each player can control only one retainer at a time. If a hero ever acquires more than one retainer, all but one of those are considered to be working at the party’s stronghold or performing some function at the periphery of any battle, not contributing meaningfully to its outcome.
Retainers are useful allies, but the heroes are always the stars of the show! Retainers are simply there to pitch in and make the heroes look good.

Retainers are simpler to run than heroes. They have fewer abilities and fewer resources to manage. Usually, a retainer makes one power roll per turn and then gets out of the way. But while a retainer’s turn is quick, it can be tactically interesting! Besides dealing damage, a retainer’s abilities often benefit their mentor or allow the mentor to do interesting things.

Because a retainer acts on their mentor’s turn, they allow the heroes’ side of an encounter to have two characters act in sequence without having to use any special abilities, providing a significant tactical advantage.

In many cases, heroes gain retainers as they acquire character features. For instance, a hero might gain a retainer from a title, a complication, or some other element of the game. When a player earns Renown, they might be able to choose a retainer as a new follower.

At other times, the events of the story can dictate that a retainer joins the party. When the heroes rescue a prisoner or befriend a former rival, you might decide that the NPC joins the party, becoming a retainer of one of the characters.
Any hero gaining a retainer is always at your discretion. If something in the rules grants a specific retainer, you can always substitute another retainer who works better for your campaign.

A retainer doesn’t need to always travel with the heroes. When they’re not called on to adventure, they can remain behind at the party’s stronghold or otherwise live their own life. Even when they’re not present, they’re still considered to be a retainer and a member of the party.

However, there might be cases when a retainer leaves the party permanently. Retainers aren’t invulnerable, so they can be killed in battle. But they can leave under less extreme circumstances as well. If the events of an adventure set a retainer against their mentor, or if the retainer’s story naturally comes to an end, you and the players can decide it’s time for the retainer to ride off into the sunset. The characters might meet their former adventuring buddy again as a friendly NPC, though—or perhaps as a foe!
When using retainers in combat, a number of special rules should be kept in mind.
Story.Body_Hanging_Leading_Colon:
Another Hero: A retainer counts as an additional hero of their current level for the purpose of encounter building (see Step-by-Step Encounte
r Building ).

Part of a Mentor’s Turn: A retainer takes their turn as part of their mentor’s turn. For the purpose of effects that end at the end of the retainer’s turn, or any other rules elements that depend on the start or end of a creature’s turn, the start and end of the mentor’s turn is also the start and end of the retainer’s turn.
Hero Can’t Act: If a hero can’t act on their turn (because they are unconscious, for example), their player can still control the hero’s retainer.
Retainer Action Economy: On their turn, a retainer can take a move action, a maneuver, and a main action, just like a hero.
Death: A retainer can become dying at 0 Stamina and die at negative half their Stamina, just like a hero.

Surges: Whenever a retainer gains surges, those surges are gained by their mentor, with the mentor and retainer sharing surges. The retainer spends surges the same way a hero can, but the extra damage granted to them by spending a surge is equal to their mentor’s highest characteristic score.
Story.Body: A retainer doesn’t earn Victories or gain XP. Instead, they usually have the same level as their mentor. When a character acquires a retainer, the retainer starts out at that mentor character’s level. Thereafter, each time a mentor gains a level, all their retainers attain the same level, whether they are actively adventuring with the hero or not.
If a character somehow acquires a retainer with a level higher than their own, the retainer doesn’t lose levels, but they don’t gain any new levels until their mentor’s level exceeds their own.

A retainer creature’s stat block includes characteristics, a level, a role, one or more abilities including a signature ability, and other standard monster features. This stat block represents the retainer’s statistics at their lowest level. The retainer’s statistics improve as they gain levels, as shown on the Retainer Advancement table.

The number of levels a retainer can gain depends on their starting level. For instance, a devil defector starts at level 5, and so can gain only 5 levels before reaching level 10. If the level noted in a retainer’s stat block is higher than 1, they don’t gain advancement benefits for any levels up to and including their starting level. As a higher-level creature, similar bonuses are already baked into their statistics.
Retainer advancement benefits are broken out as follows:
Story.Body_Hanging_Leading_Colon: Characteristic Increase: At level 2, a retainer increases one of their characteristic scores by 1 (to a maximum of 2). At level 5, they increase each of their characteristic scores by 1 (to a maximum of 3), and at level 8, they increase one characteristic score by 1 (to a maximum of 4). For each single-characteristic increase, the player of the retainer’s mentor chooses which characteristic to use.
Free Strike Damage Bonus: The retainer gains a +2 damage bonus to free strikes at level 3, at level 6, and at level 9.

Advancement Abilities: A retainer gains new abilities at levels 4, 7, and 10 (unless the retainer’s starting level is that level or higher). Each retainer stat block is accompanied by retainer advancement abilities specific to that retainer. Whenever a retainer would gain a new advancement ability, instead of choosing their retainer ability, the player of their mentor can instead choose a role advancement ability that matches their role and level. (Advancement abilities for each type of creature role are detailed in the next section.)
Stamina Bonus: At each level, a retainer gains a +9 bonus to Stamina.

Signature Ability Damage Increase: A retainer’s signature ability is unique in that it grows stronger as the retainer advances in level. Only the retainer’s signature ability improves this way! The table features two columns for a retainer’s signature ability damage bonus—one for a tier 1 power roll outcome and one for a tier 2 or tier 3 outcome. A retainer’s signature ability gains a +1 damage bonus every second level for a tier 1 outcome, and every level for a tier 2 or tier 3 outcome.
Story.Body: A 4th-level hero convinces a goblin guide, a level 1 harrier retainer, to join the party. The goblin guide immediately jumps to level 4. For level 2, the guide increases their Agility by 1. For level 3, the guide gains a +2 damage bonus to their free strikes. For level 4, the guide chooses between the level 4 retainer advancement ability Weaving Knives or the level 4 harrier advancement ability Tackle (see below).

Additionally, for jumping from level 1 to level 4, the guide gains a +27 bonus to Stamina, giving them Stamina 48. Their signature ability gains a +2 damage bonus on a tier 1 outcome (for a total of 5 damage), and a +3 bonus on a tier 2 outcome (8 damage) or a tier 3 outcome (10 damage).
Some retainer abilities have the Encounter keyword. Once a retainer uses an encounter ability, they can’t use that ability again until their mentor earns a Victory.

This book includes more than a dozen retainer stat blocks with advancement information. But most creature stat blocks can be turned into retainers, provided a creature isn’t a minion, a leader, or a solo. You have the final say over whether a player can choose a specific creature as a custom retainer.

To turn a creature into a custom retainer, start with the creature’s stat block. Instead of the Stamina noted in the stat block, a custom retainer has 21 Stamina at level 1. Then use the Retainer Advancement table as a guide to adjusting the creature’s statistics as they increase in level, including starting at higher than level 1.

If the creature’s signature ability affects an area or targets more than one creature or object, the ability now only affects one target within distance. A custom retainer has no retainer advancement abilities, so they must take the role advancement ability specific to their level and role. Custom retainers can’t use any abilities or effects that require Malice.

A 4th-level hero trains a striped condor griffon, a level 2 elite brute, gaining that noble creature as a retainer. The griffon starts as a level 2 retainer. They have Stamina 30 (21 for level 1 and a +9 bonus for being level 2). Because they started at level 2, they don’t gain any level 2 benefits or advancement features from the Retainer Advancement table.

When a retainer reaches level 4, 7, or 10, they can gain one of the following abilities based on their role, rather than gaining the retainer advancement ability presented alongside their stat block. A retainer qualifies only for the role advancement ability that matches their role and level.

If a role advancement ability has the Magic or Psionic keyword, a retainer can swap the Magic keyword for Psionic or vice versa. They can also lose the keyword if they can achieve the ability’s effects through gadgetry, martial prowess, or other nonsupernatural means.

The light-grey-skinned, wavy silver-haired devil stands, half-shadowed, red eyes glowing, in a snow-dusted rocky alcove wearing crimson robes with a jagged silver trim beneath a silver breastplate patterned with pointed scales, curved at the top. Their red, scaled tail, covered in spines, curls around in a spiral toward their left, the tip pointing at their silver-tipped shoes. Their raised right arm has a spike on their elbow, and glints with the dusky light, holds a rapier pointing downward. The handle and crossguard are thorned, curving vines, and the blade is barbed. A helix of blood echoing the curve of their tail and the handle swirls magically upward around it, bouncing a deep red across their entire left side.
